q-1477.name: Question 1
q-1477.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
¬(P⇒Q)≡¬(¬P∨Q).
$$

We can distribute the negation over the disjunction using De Morgan's law:

$$
¬(¬P∨Q)≡¬(¬P)∧¬Q.
$$

Finally, canceling out double negations, we reach

$$
¬(¬P)∧¬Q≡P∧¬Q.
$$

So the given statement is equivalent to $P∧¬Q.$

q-182498.worked_solution:
The conditional statement $P⇒Q$ is logically equivalent to the disjunction $¬P∨Q:$

q-182591.name: Question 4
q-182591.problem:
$\,$ Pay the bill, or your power will be shut off.

Which conditional statement is logically equivalent to the disjunctive statement above?
q-182591.worked_solution:
Let's denote by $A$ and $B$ the following statements:

- $A:$ Pay the bill.

- $B:$ Your power will be shut off.

Then, our initial statement can be written as $A∨B,$ which is logically equivalent to 

$$
¬A⇒B.
$$

The negation of $A$ can be written as

- $¬A:$ You don't pay the bill.

Therefore, the given statement is logically equivalent to the following:

$\,$ If you don't pay the bill, then your power will be shut off.
